intro.author: Habakkuk the prophet (1:1); nothing is known of his life beyond this book
intro.written: Probably about 610–600 BC, as Babylon (the Chaldeans) was rising to power
intro.audience: Judah, overhearing a prophet's honest conversation with God
intro.setting: After good King Josiah died in 609 BC, Judah slid back into violence and injustice under King Jehoiakim. Meanwhile Babylon defeated Assyria and Egypt and was becoming the dominant power. Habakkuk wrestles with why God allows evil, and why he would use a nation even more wicked than Judah to punish it.
intro.purpose: To show a believer bringing hard questions to God, receiving his answer, and learning to trust and rejoice in him even when circumstances collapse.
intro.bigIdea: 'The just shall live by his faith,' trusting God's timing and justice even when it is hard to see.
